Philip Rivers lost a high school playoff game on Friday night, and today he is taking over an ACC program.

St. Michael Catholic in Fairhope, Alabama lost at home to The Glenwood School, 42 to 35. That was the end of their season.

Two days later NC State is finalizing a deal to make him their head coach, according to Chris Low, Pete Nakos and Noah Fleischman.

He has run that high school since 2021. Semifinals in each of the last two seasons, and no state title in any of them.

NC State fired Dave Doeren after 14 seasons. Doeren is the winningest football coach the school has ever had.

So they are handing the job to a man whose last game was a 42 to 35 loss in the Alabama playoffs.

The quarterback he was coaching in that game is his son.

Gunner Rivers is a four star and a top 10 quarterback in the 2027 class. He committed to NC State months ago, long before his father was a candidate for anything. He will be on the roster next season.

Which means Rivers coached his son in high school and now gets to keep coaching him in the ACC.

That is the same thing his own father did to him.

Steve Rivers coached high school football in Alabama. When Steve took the job at Athens High, Philip went with him and played for his dad.

Steve wore number 17 when he was a high school player.

Philip wore 17 for his entire career because of it. College, San Diego, Indianapolis, all of it. He played 17 seasons in the NFL in his father's number.

Now his son will play for him at the school where Philip played.

A reporter asked Rivers on Friday whether the NC State conversations were going to lead somewhere.

"There could be," he said.

He talked about his family being settled in south Alabama, about ten kids and grandchildren, about what a move would cost them.

He was asked whether coaching Gunner in college was the deciding piece.

"Should it come to that, I wouldn't call that the deciding factor."

Then he talked about his quarterback, who had been banged up most of the year.

"I thought he played pretty dang good, to be honest with you."

He has never coached a college game. He has never been a coordinator. He has never been a position coach in college, or a graduate assistant, or an analyst.

He has been a high school head coach in a town of 25,000 people for five years, and on Friday his season ended at home.

TODAY he is reportedly the next head coach at North Carolina State, where he will coach the quarterback he has been coaching since the kid was old enough to hold a ball.
